lesson.3_1.title: The emergency fund
lesson.3_1.gut.prompt: Your phone screen breaks. The repair costs ₹2,800. You have ₹500 saved. What do you do?
lesson.3_1.gut.bridge: Surprises will come. An emergency fund turns them into small problems.
lesson.3_1.gut.a.label: Borrow from a moneylender
lesson.3_1.gut.a.result: You get the money today. At 10% a month, that is ₹280 of interest every month until you repay.
lesson.3_1.gut.b.label: Take it from the money saved for your goal
lesson.3_1.gut.b.result: The phone is fixed, and your goal moves further away.
lesson.3_1.gut.c.label: Live with the cracked screen for now
lesson.3_1.gut.c.result: No debt. But the problem stays, and a real emergency could not wait.
lesson.3_1.c1.text: Some costs do not wait for a good month: a broken screen, an illness, a lost week of pay.
lesson.3_1.c2.text: An emergency fund is money kept aside only for surprises like these. It is a buffer between you and a loan.
lesson.3_1.c3.text: How big? Adults often aim for 3 to 6 months of their expenses. In this game, one month is counted as ₹3,000. That figure is an assumption for the game.
lesson.3_1.c3.reveal.prompt: You have ₹4,500 in your emergency fund. How many months does it cover in this game?
lesson.3_1.c4.text: It must be easy to reach. Liquidity means how quickly something turns into cash without losing value.
lesson.3_1.c4.sort.prompt: Is this a good home for an emergency fund?
lesson.3_1.c4.sort.yes: Yes: safe and easy to reach
lesson.3_1.c4.sort.locked: A deposit locked for a year
lesson.3_1.c4.sort.feedback: An emergency fund is not there to grow. It is there to be there.
lesson.3_1.c5.text: Without a fund, a surprise becomes a debt, or it eats the money saved for a goal.
lesson.3_1.c6.text: Build it a little every month. After you use it, fill it again first.
lesson.3_1.q1.prompt: What is an emergency fund for?
lesson.3_1.q1.right: Yes. It is for surprises, not for wants.
lesson.3_1.q1.wrong: It is for costs you could not plan for. A sale is a want, and growth comes later.
lesson.3_1.q1.o2: Costs you did not plan for, like a repair or an illness
lesson.3_1.q2.prompt: An emergency fund belongs where it can earn the most, even if it is locked for years.
lesson.3_1.q2.right: Correct, it's false. An emergency cannot wait for a lock to open.
lesson.3_1.q2.wrong: It's false. This money has to be easy to reach. Liquidity matters more than growth here.
lesson.3_1.q3.prompt: In this game one month is counted as ₹3,000. Your fund has ₹6,000. How many months are covered?
lesson.3_1.q3.wrong: Divide the fund by one month's amount: ₹6,000 ÷ ₹3,000 = 2 months.
lesson.3_1.effect: Your Emergency fund opens, with a meter that shows how many months it covers. It counts towards your Money Health Score.
lesson.3_2.title: Insurance in plain words
lesson.3_2.gut.prompt: A hospital bill of ₹60,000 arrives for a family. With health insurance or without: what changes?
lesson.3_2.gut.bridge: Insurance is paying a little so that one big loss cannot break you.
lesson.3_2.gut.a.label: Without insurance
lesson.3_2.gut.a.result: The whole ₹60,000 comes from savings, or from a loan.
lesson.3_2.gut.b.label: With insurance
lesson.3_2.gut.b.result: The family has been paying a small premium. The insurer now pays most of the bill.
lesson.3_2.gut.c.label: "It won't happen to us"
lesson.3_2.gut.c.result: Most years it does not. Insurance is for the one year it does.
lesson.3_2.c1.text: Some losses are too big for any emergency fund: a long hospital stay, or the death of the person who earns.
lesson.3_2.c2.text: With insurance you pay a small amount regularly, called the premium. In return the insurer pays if a named loss happens.
lesson.3_2.c3.text: The most the insurer will pay is the sum assured. Asking the insurer to pay is making a claim.
lesson.3_2.c4.text: Health insurance pays hospital bills. Term insurance pays the family a sum if the insured person dies.
lesson.3_2.c4.sort.fever: A week in hospital with fever
lesson.3_2.c4.sort.loan: A home loan left unpaid after a death
lesson.3_2.c4.sort.feedback: Each kind of insurance covers one kind of loss. Read what a policy pays for.
lesson.3_2.c5.text: Term plans pay only if the insured person dies. Endowment plans also pay a maturity amount, but usually cost more for the same cover.
lesson.3_2.c6.text: Tell the insurer the truth about your health when you buy. This is called disclosure. A hidden fact can get a claim rejected.
lesson.3_2.c7.text: In this game, health cover costs ₹150 a month. That is ₹1,800 a year. If you fall ill, you pay ₹500 and the cover pays the rest.
lesson.3_2.q1.right: Yes. The premium is the price of the protection.
lesson.3_2.q1.wrong: The premium is what you pay. What the insurer pays, up to a limit, is the claim amount.
lesson.3_2.q1.o1: The amount the insurer pays you
lesson.3_2.q1.o2: The amount you pay regularly for the cover
lesson.3_2.q2.prompt: A term plan pays a maturity amount even if nothing happens to the insured person.
lesson.3_2.q2.right: Correct, it's false. A term plan pays only on death. That is why its premium is lower.
lesson.3_2.q2.wrong: It's false. Term plans pay only if the insured person dies. Endowment plans pay a maturity amount and usually cost more.
lesson.3_2.q3.prompt: Why tell the insurer the truth about your health?
lesson.3_2.q3.right: Right. Honest disclosure is what makes a claim hold up.
lesson.3_2.q3.wrong: If you hide something, the insurer can refuse to pay when you need it most.
lesson.3_2.q3.o1: It lowers the premium every time
lesson.3_2.q3.o2: A hidden fact can get a claim rejected
lesson.3_2.effect: You decide: buy health cover or skip it. Cover costs ₹150 every month. If illness strikes, it cuts your cost to ₹500.
lesson.3_3.title: Recurring deposit: the saving-habit machine
lesson.3_3.gut.prompt: You can lock ₹500 a month for 6 months at about 6.5% a year. Or keep it all in your wallet. What do you do?
lesson.3_3.gut.bridge: Saving is easier when it happens by itself. Meet the recurring deposit.
lesson.3_3.gut.a.label: Lock it in a recurring deposit
lesson.3_3.gut.a.result: After 6 months you get about ₹3,057 back. You cannot use it for surprises on the way.
lesson.3_3.gut.b.label: Keep it in my wallet
lesson.3_3.gut.b.result: It stays free to use. It is also easy to spend, and it earns nothing.
lesson.3_3.gut.c.label: Lock everything I have
lesson.3_3.gut.c.result: A strong habit, but nothing is left for an emergency. Locked money cannot help you this week.
lesson.3_3.c1.text: Saving "whatever is left" at the end of the month often means saving nothing.
lesson.3_3.c2.text: A recurring deposit, or RD, takes a fixed amount every month for a fixed time. Each payment is an instalment.
lesson.3_3.c3.text: At the end, on maturity, you get back everything you put in, plus interest.
lesson.3_3.c3.reveal.prompt: ₹500 a month for 6 months at 6.5% a year. What comes back?
lesson.3_3.c3.reveal.answer: About ₹3,057: your ₹3,000, plus about ₹57 of interest.
lesson.3_3.c4.text: The interest is small. The habit is the real prize: the money is saved before you can spend it.
lesson.3_3.c5.text: An RD is locked. Close it early and you earn less. Miss an instalment and there is a fee. In this game the fee is ₹50.
lesson.3_3.c5.sort.trip: Money for a trip 6 months away
lesson.3_3.c5.sort.laptop: Money for a laptop next year
lesson.3_3.c5.sort.fees: Money for a bill due this week
lesson.3_3.c5.sort.feedback: An RD suits a goal with a date. An emergency has no date.
lesson.3_3.c6.text: So the order matters: a small emergency fund first, then an RD for your goals.
lesson.3_3.q1.right: Yes. A fixed instalment, every month, until maturity.
lesson.3_3.q1.wrong: An RD takes the same amount every month for a fixed time. One big deposit is a fixed deposit, which comes later.
lesson.3_3.q1.o1: One big deposit locked for years
lesson.3_3.q1.o2: A fixed amount saved every month for a fixed time
lesson.3_3.q2.prompt: An RD is a good place for your emergency money.
lesson.3_3.q2.right: Correct, it's false. An RD is locked, and an emergency cannot wait.
lesson.3_3.q2.wrong: It's false. RD money is locked until maturity. Emergency money must be easy to reach.
lesson.3_3.q3.right: Right. On maturity you receive your instalments plus the interest.
lesson.3_3.q3.wrong: Maturity is the end of the deposit's time, when you get your money back with interest.
lesson.3_3.q3.o1: The day the deposit ends and the money comes back with interest
lesson.3_3.q3.o2: The fee for missing an instalment
lesson.3_3.effect: Your RD bucket opens. Once you start one, its instalment leaves your wallet every month before anything else.
